title: Propellerhead Reason, 2000
lede: Music software drawn as a studio equipment rack, with a back panel of animated patch cables.
summary: A virtual rack of synthesizers and effects with riveted panels and patch cables. Propellerhead, 2000.

source.label: Sound On Sound, Derek Johnson and Debbie Poyser, review (March 2001)

evidence.note: No image was inspected. Based on the Sound On Sound review (March 2001) and Wikipedia.

styles.note: The audio branch of the style: hardware imitated down to rack rails, rivets, knobs, and cables. It predates the Apple period and continued through it.

context: Reason first released in 2000. “Reason simulates a recording studio with virtual cables and representations of a subtractive synthesizer, sampler and drum machine.” [Wikipedia: Reason Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reason_Studios).

Sound On Sound: devices “appear as graphic units in a rack”; “flipping the on-screen image reveals a back-panel view of the virtual hardware, complete with animated pluggable cabling.” Audio cables are red, effects cables green, and Gate and CV leads yellow. The mixer’s look “owes a lot to Mackie’s LM3204.” [Sound On Sound, March 2001](https://www.soundonsound.com/reviews/propellerhead-software-reason).

Wikipedia’s skeuomorph article names audio software that emulates “physical musical instruments and audio equipment complete with buttons and dials” as an extreme example. [Wikipedia: Skeuomorph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skeuomorph).
interpretation: Here the metaphor carries function: the cable view is how users route signals. It is the strongest case for the style’s claim that familiar objects teach.
